items.html:
One remaining concrete defect:

  • P2 — Constant framework directions unnecessarily require side. _framework_waves.py:300 equates backend ownership with active differentiation. Consequently, a PyTorch direction tensor with requires_grad=False is considered variable, and _framework_smatrix.py:201–204 rejects network.power(incident) unless users specify side. The identical direction supplied as a list succeeds. Distinguish constant framework arrays from tracers/gradient-bearing tensors, retaining backend ownership separately.

Reproducer, executed with CPU threads capped at one:

thickness = torch.tensor(0.2, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
network = tr.slab(
    basis=tr.PlaneWavePorts.default([[0, 0]]),
    k0=1.2, thickness=thickness, material=3,
)
incident = tr.plane_wave(
    torch.tensor([0., 0., 1.], dtype=torch.float64),
    "positive_helicity", k0=1.2,
)
network.power(incident)  # ValueError; list direction works

The scalar polarization-label incompatibility I reported earlier is already fixed in current source.

No context-ownership, replay, complex-cotangent, or mixed-backend corruption defect found in the reviewed Autograd implementation. Dispatch/promotion separation and unified Material provide a coherent abstraction without a new registry or ambient backend state.

Executed probes confirmed batched NumPy/Torch waves both preserve (modes, illuminations) inputs and corresponding field shapes. Ordinary API coverage still has explicit gaps, including framework Wave.modetype and PeriodicResponse.scatter; avoid describing every root method as supported unless those are addressed.

Read-only review; no files or Git state changed.

The Rust failure is a preexisting single-thread test defect exposed by the capped environment, not a regression from this Python change.

  • fpenv.rs:564 calls parallel::try_map(..., true) in its “on workers” helper.
  • parallel.rs:186 instead executes inline when the thread budget is one.
  • fpenv.rs:610 calls that helper on a deliberately flushing caller outside the IEEE guard. Zeros are therefore expected, contradicting its assertion at line 616. The worker-mode and guarded-result assertions immediately before it pass.

Both source sections match baseline fcf62400700e326ffcc61ec50025cb25ea43ea6d; there are no Rust changes. I reproduced the failure using the existing binary with all thread budgets set to one. The focused guarded-LU test passes under the same settings. No builds or edits performed.

The python/AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md edits are appropriately scoped: they add Autograd to the optional-backend guidance and identify the new dispatch boundary. No unnecessary process or policy changes.
